Rashi on Taanit 5a:10:1.english: That which was in the fields - Aftergrowths and that which remained in the fields.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:10:2.english: They ate the flesh of their sons - some of them.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:11:1.hebrew: משום דבקרבך קדוש – שאתה מטיב מעשיך, לא יבא הקב"ה בעיר:
Rashi on Taanit 5a:11:1.english: Because it is sacred in your midst - [meaning] that you improve your deeds, will the Holy One, blessed be He, not enter the city?

Rashi on Taanit 5a:11:2.hebrew: לא אבא בירושלים כו' – והכי קאמר, עד שיהא בקרבך קדוש למטה — דהיינו ירושלים — לא אבוא בעיר שלמעלה:
Rashi on Taanit 5a:11:2.english: I shall not enter Jerusalem, etc. - And this is what [the verse] means: Until "it is sacred in your midst" below — that is, Jerusalem — I will not enter the city above.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:12:1.hebrew: ירושלים הבנויה כעיר שחוברה לה יחדיו – ירושלים שלמטה תהא בנויה כעיר שחוברה לה, שהיא כיוצא בה, חבירתה ודוגמתה. מכלל דאיכא ירושלים אחריתי, והיכן, אם לא למעלה:
Rashi on Taanit 5a:12:1.english: Jerusalem that is built as a city that is joined together - The Jerusalem below will be built like a city that is joined to it, which is like it, its counterpart and its likeness. This implies that there is another Jerusalem; and where is it, if not above?

Rashi on Taanit 5a:13:1.hebrew: ובאחת יבערו ויכסלו מוסר הבלים עץ הוא - אי לאו גזרה שוה, היה משמע אטומים כעץ לקבל מוסר, ולשוא היו לוקין:
Rashi on Taanit 5a:13:1.english: And with one they are brutish and foolish, the teaching of vanities is wood - Were it not for the verbal analogy (gezerah shavah), it would imply [that they are] impervious like wood to receiving rebuke, and they would be smitten in vain.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:13:2.english: With one - [Through one] transgression that they commit, the fools—[that is,] the wicked—will be burned.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:14:1.hebrew: עשרים וארבע שביקא להו – בתמיה. בפרשת התשפוט (יחזקאל כב) כ"ד עבירות שעברו. ל"א: שעברו על כ"ד ספרים:
Rashi on Taanit 5a:14:1.english: Twenty-four [are] abandoned - [This is] a rhetorical question: in the passage "Will you judge" (Ezekiel 22), [there are] twenty-four transgressions that they committed. Another version: That they transgressed against [the] twenty-four books [of Scripture].

Rashi on Taanit 5a:1:1.hebrew: רבא אמר כיון שהתחיל - בשמיני ספק שביעי, שוב אינו פוסק:
Rashi on Taanit 5a:1:1.english: Rava said: Once one has started - [to mention rain] on the eighth [day], which is possibly the seventh, he no longer stops.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:2:1.english: He retracted – from what he said: "he stops."

Rashi on Taanit 5a:2:2.hebrew: מונה כ"א יום - מראש השנה עד שמיני ספק שביעי של חג, כדרך שמונה מר"ה עד יוה"כ י' ימים, שמתחיל למנות מיום ראשון של ר"ה, ומזכיר מכאן ואילך. וזהו שמזכיר בשמיני ספק שביעי, שהוא כ"ב, שוב אינו פוסק. והא דמתחילין אנו למנות מיום א', דהא דאנו עושין ב' ימים לאו משום ספק דשמא עיברו לאלול, דהא אנן בקיאינן בקביעא דירחא, אלא משום דמנהג אבותינו בידינו. ל"א: מונה כ"א יום כדרך שמונה כו', כלומר: אם עיברו אלול, לא יחשוב מיום ראשון של ר"ה כ"א יום, שאם כן לא ימצאו בידו אלא כ', וכלים ביום טוב שביעי, יום נטילת ערבה; אלא מיום שמתחילין למנות עשרה ימים לעשות בעשירי יוה"כ, יתחיל למנות באלו, שבכך לא יטעה, שיום הכפורים יום אחד לבד, וידע מהיכן התחילו למנות לו. וביום שכלין כ"א, דהיינו ביום טוב אחרון, מתחיל להזכיר, וכיון שהתחיל שוב אינו פוסק:
Rashi on Taanit 5a:2:2.english: One counts twenty-one days - From Rosh HaShana until the eighth [day], [which is] possibly the seventh [day], of the Festival [of Sukkot], just as one counts ten days from Rosh HaShana until Yom Kippur, for one begins counting from the first day of Rosh HaShana and mentions [rain] from then on. And this is [why] when one mentions [rain] on the eighth [day], [which is] possibly the seventh [day] — which is the twenty-second [day from the first day of Rosh HaShana] — he no longer stops. And [the reason] that we begin counting from the first day [is] because [the fact] that we observe two days [of Rosh HaShana] is not due to doubt lest they intercalated Elul — for we are expert in the fixing of the [new] moon — rather, [it is] because the custom of our ancestors is in our hands. Another explanation: "One counts twenty-one days just as one counts, etc." — that is to say, if they intercalated Elul, one should not count twenty-one days from the first day of Rosh HaShana, for if so, only twenty [days of Tishrei] would be found in his hand, and they would end on the seventh day of the Festival, the day of taking the willow; rather, from the day that they begin to count ten days to observe Yom Kippur on the tenth, he shall begin to count for these [twenty-one days], for thereby he will not err, since Yom Kippur is one day only, and he will know from where they began to count for it. And on the day that the twenty-one [days] end — which is on the last Festival day — he begins to mention [rain], and once he has begun, he no longer stops.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:4:1.hebrew: א"ל רב נחמן לרב יצחק יורה בניסן הוא - דכתיב "ויורד לכם גשם מורה ומלקוש בראשון", בתמיה:
Rashi on Taanit 5a:4:1.english: Rav Nachman said to Rav Yitzchak: Is the first rain in Nisan? - Since it is written, "And He causes to come down for you the rain, the former rain and the latter rain in the first [month]," [he asks this] in astonishment.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:4:2.english: But it is in Marcheshvan – As it is taught [in a baraita] later on, and it is in the Sifrei.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:4:3.english: The first rain [yoreh] and the last rain [malkosh] - [The Gemara] explains [them] later.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:4:4.hebrew: אמר ליה - ודאי במרחשון הוא, ומקרא זה בימי יואל בן פתואל נתקיים, שיורה ומלקוש היה בראשון ע"י נס, שהיה רעב שבע שנים, דכתיב: "כי קרא ה' לרעב וגם בא אל הארץ שבע שנים", וכתיב: "יתר הגזם אכל הארבה וגו'":
Rashi on Taanit 5a:4:4.english: He said to him - Certainly it is in Marcheshvan, and this verse was fulfilled in the days of Joel son of Pethuel, [meaning] that the early rain and the late rain were in the first [month] through a miracle; for there was a famine of seven years, as it is written: "For the Lord has called for a famine, and it has also come upon the land seven years," and it is written: "That which the palmer-worm has left, the locust has eaten, etc."

Rashi on Taanit 5a:4:5.english: This is how we read [the text]: "Adar ended and no rain had fallen" - and we do not read "and they did not sow [during] most of Adar."

Rashi on Taanit 5a:4:6.hebrew: רביעה ראשונה – התחלת גשמים, ולקמן (תענית דף ו:) מפרש רביעה, שמרביע את הארץ:
Rashi on Taanit 5a:4:6.english: First rainfall - The beginning of the rains; and later (Taanit 6b) [the Gemara] explains [the term] revi'ah, that it fructifies the earth.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:5:1.hebrew: או יזרענו וימות – ברעב קודם שתגדל התבואה החדשה, שלא יהיה לו מה יאכל:
Rashi on Taanit 5a:5:1.english: Or sow it and die - Of starvation, before the new grain grows, as he will have nothing to eat.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:5:2.english: A miracle occurred for them, etc. - And this is what is written: "And I will restore to you the years that the locust has eaten, etc."

Rashi on Taanit 5a:5:3.english: Grain in ant holes and that which was in the walls was revealed to them - Which the mice had stored.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:6:1.english: They went out and sowed - And they sowed what was in their hands.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:6:2.hebrew: שני - בניסן, ושלישי ורביעי. ומה שמצאו אכלו, ולאחר שזרעו ירדו להם גשמים בה' בניסן, והקריבו עומר בט"ז בניסן מאותה תבואה חדשה:
Rashi on Taanit 5a:6:2.english: [On the] second - of Nisan, and [on the] third and fourth. And what they found, they ate; and after they sowed, rains fell for them on the fifth of Nisan, and they offered [the] omer on the sixteenth of Nisan from that new grain.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:6:3.english: That grows in six months - From Tishrei until Nisan.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:6:4.hebrew: בי"א יום – מחמשה בניסן עד ט"ז בו:
Rashi on Taanit 5a:6:4.english: In eleven days - From the fifth of Nisan until the sixteenth of it.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:7:1.english: They who sow in tears shall reap with joy - For they had nothing to eat.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:7:2.hebrew: מאי הלך ילך ובכה - אם לבני אדם, כבר נאמר "הזורעים בדמעה ברנה יקצורו", אלא על השור הכתוב אומר:
Rashi on Taanit 5a:7:2.english: What is [the meaning of] "Though he goes on his way weeping" - If [it refers] to human beings, it has already been stated, "They who sow in tears shall reap with joy"; rather, Scripture is speaking about the ox.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:7:3.english: On its way - to plow the furrow.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:7:4.hebrew: ובחזירתו אוכל חזיז – שחת מן התלם שזרעו בהליכתן, שכשהוא זורע, מיד מתחלת ליגדל:
Rashi on Taanit 5a:7:4.english: And upon its return, it eats chaziz - Young green shoots from the furrow that they sowed on their way out, for when he sows, it immediately begins to grow.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:8:1.hebrew: מאי בא יבוא ברנה נושא אלומותיו – אם מפני התבואה שיש להם לאכול, הרי כבר אמור ברנה יקצורו:
Rashi on Taanit 5a:8:1.english: What is [the meaning of] "He shall surely come with rejoicing, bearing his sheaves" - If [it is] because of the grain that they have to eat, behold, it is already stated, "With rejoicing they shall reap."

Rashi on Taanit 5a:8:2.hebrew: שבולת זרתים – זהו נס גדול, מה שאין כן דרך כל תבואה, שהקנה פי שלשה וארבעה בשבולת:
Rashi on Taanit 5a:8:2.english: An ear two spans - This is a great miracle, unlike the way of all [ordinary] grain, where the stalk is three or four times [the length of] the ear.

Rashi on Taanit 5a:9:1.english: For the Lord has called upon a famine - [This] was said in the days of Jehoram son of Ahab.

Tosafot on Taanit 5a:11:1.hebrew: לא אבוא בעיר - פירוש: "בעיר" ר"ל בעיר ממש. וי"מ פשטיה דקרא: "בעיר" — בשנאה, כלומר לא אבוא בשנאה, ו"עיר" הוי ל' שנאה, כמו "ומלאו פני תבל ערים" (ישעיהו יד):
Tosafot on Taanit 5a:11:1.english: "I will not enter the city (be'ir)" - Explanation: "be'ir" means in an actual city. And some explain the plain meaning of the verse to be that "be'ir" means with hatred, that is to say, "I will not come with hatred," for "ir" is an expression of hatred, as in, "and fill the face of the world with enemies (arim)" (Isaiah 14).

Tosafot on Taanit 5a:1:1.hebrew: רבא אמר כיון שהתחיל שוב אינו פוסק - כלומר: כיון שהתחיל ביום ראשון של אחרונים, שוב אינו פוסק; וכן הפסק:
Tosafot on Taanit 5a:1:1.english: Rava said: Once one has started, he no longer stops - That is to say: once one has started [mentioning rain] on the first day of the last [days of the festival], he no longer stops; and so is the ruling.

Tosafot on Taanit 5a:4:1.hebrew: יורה במרחשון הוא - פי': אקרא דכתיב "ויורד לכם גשם מורה ומלקוש בראשון" פריך; דמתני' אפשר לתרץ דאמלקוש קסמיך, אבל ביורה מודה דבמרחשון:
Tosafot on Taanit 5a:4:1.english: "The first rain is in Marḥeshvan" - Explanation: [Rav Naḥman] is raising an objection from the verse that is written: "And He causes to come down for you the rain, the former rain [moreh] and the latter rain [malkosh] in the first [month]" (Joel 2:23); for [as for] the Mishnah, it is possible to resolve [it by saying] that it relies on [the mention of] the latter rain [malkosh], whereas regarding the former rain [yoreh], it agrees that [it falls] in Marḥeshvan.

Tosafot on Taanit 5a:7:1.hebrew: ובחזירתו אוכל חזיז מן התלם וכו' - וקשיא: הא דקאמר לעיל "נמצא הגדילה בששה חדשים גדילה באחד עשר יום", הוה ליה למימר "גדילה בתליסר ובי"ד יומי", שהרי מיד מתחלת ליגדל. ושמא י"ל דלכל המאוחרת שנזרעה בשלישית קאמר "נמצא גדילה בי"א יום", וצ"ע:
Tosafot on Taanit 5a:7:1.english: And upon its return, it eats young shoots [ḥaziz] from the furrow, etc. - And this is difficult: [regarding] what it said earlier, "Consequently, [grain] that grows in six months grew in eleven days," it should have said, "[grew] in thirteen or fourteen days," since it begins to grow immediately. And perhaps one can say that it is speaking of the latest [grain], which was sown on the third [day of sowing], [when it says,] "Consequently, it grew in eleven days," and this requires further study.
